settings.title: Building PHAM, from the beginning.
settings.lead: I started PHAM at sixteen, without a team or an industry network. This is the work behind Edition 01.
settings.present_heading: The first edition is still being built.
settings.present_body_1: PHAM-001 is still being refined. I want its specifications, changes and production decisions to be clear before the release.
settings.present_body_2: I cannot promise a sellout. I can keep improving the object and be transparent about what I can deliver.

settings.title: There was no head start.
settings.body_1: I began PHAM in 2026 at sixteen, still in high school, without investors, a team or fashion contacts.
settings.body_2: With limited funds, I had to learn materials, construction and manufacturing language before I could give precise instructions to a workshop.

settings.title: A DESIGN THAT CAN BE MADE.
settings.body_1: PHAM-001 began as a cropped bomber with structured shoulders, contrasting panels and adjustable details. Turning a sketch into a technical specification was the real challenge.
settings.body_2: I worked with an overseas workshop from Vietnam. Measurements and references had to be precise; a vague instruction could cost time and money.

settings.title: THE FIRST SAMPLE WAS NOT FINAL.
settings.body_1: The first sample made the design tangible. Its silhouette and workmanship gave me reason to continue.
settings.body_2: The lookbook also exposed what needed work: surfaces that looked too flat and panels less defined than intended. Another sample meant more cost, but the first version was not finished.

settings.title: The work people rarely see.
settings.body_1: The jacket was only one part of PHAM. I also built the website, packaging, size information, edition identity and customer communications.
settings.body_2: I balanced this work with school and limited funds. I focused on what I could verify and made clear what was still in development.

settings.title: EARNING TRUST, ONE JACKET AT A TIME.
settings.body_1: Fifty jackets is a small edition but a serious commitment for an unknown label. Each buyer needs a reason to trust the garment and the process.
settings.body_2: A sellout is not guaranteed. Production and marketing cost money, and interest is not an order. I would rather show the work than promise success.

settings.title: CAPITAL & CASH FLOW
settings.body: Samples, revisions, packaging and production require capital before delivery. Some decisions must wait.

settings.title: DISTANCE & COMMUNICATION
settings.body: Working with an overseas workshop from Vietnam requires precise references and physical sample reviews.

settings.title: TIME & RESPONSIBILITY
settings.body: School and exams continue alongside design, sourcing and running the store.

settings.title: EARNING TRUST
settings.body: An unknown label earns trust through clear specifications, honest progress and transparent release conditions.
